answer: A hardware-rooted attestation protocol forces each agent to anchor its identity within an isolated secure enclave while bonding funds in a tiered stake terrace. An attacker must expend scarce physical cryptographic silicon and lock verifiable liquidity for every persona, making a gale of fabricated nodes prohibitively expensive. However, this relies on centralized chip fabricators as roots of trust and risks systemic failure if enclave firmware contains unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities.
